html:
SMTO-CTX-0018 — SMTO stopped this task because its saved steps don't line up

GUID: aba5e655-35be-4b7c-a4a9-23bf7a33e575
Slug: context-transcript-invalid
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • Before asking the AI model for its next step, SMTO checks that every action in the task has its matching result. That record is out of order, so the task stopped. Actions it already carried out may have taken effect.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the stopped task in the conversation and read its activity to see which steps finished before it stopped. The error alone does not establish which steps finished, and the task may already have run commands or changed files.
  2. Look directly at the files, systems or items the task was working on and note which changes are already there. Asking for a change that already happened could make it twice.
  3. Start a new task that asks only for the work that is still missing. This task's saved record can't be used for another model request, but a new task starts with a clean record.
  4. Open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. This problem comes from SMTO itself, and the copied details show which check failed.

What success looks like

  • The new task runs and finishes without this message, and you have confirmed nothing was done twice.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Send the copied error details and your SMTO version to the person who installed or manages SMTO. Don't delete the stopped task or its conversation; its saved record is needed to find the cause.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Provider-message validation rejected the stored task transcript: a tool result has no matching pending call, pending tool calls lack results, tool-call IDs repeat, a role is unsupported, or the leading system message or real user query is missing.

What this means

  • The provider transcript must retain its leading instructions and user query, supported roles and one matching result for each pending tool call; the stored sequence violates those invariants. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The provider transcript must retain its leading instructions and user query, supported roles and one matching result for each pending tool call; the stored sequence violates those invariants.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect unmatched or duplicate call IDs and role ordering in the retained transcript alongside authoritative receipts; do not replay work to repair message structure.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Treat this as a defect: read the validate_correlations or validate_provider_messages message in the Server log or Technical details and keep the run, its saved state and receipts unchanged for diagnosis. Do not hand-edit the transcript, insert placeholder tool results, or replay recorded operations to make it pass; report the error ID with the installed SMTO version.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The retained transcript passes role and correlation validation with genuine results for its recorded calls.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
